analysis:
The PR changes docs/architecture/inference.md only: it bumps the 'Last updated' date (head line 3) and adds a paragraph at head lines 253-259. That paragraph says the SSD prefix-cache staging stage runs before engine.submit, off the engine queue, and that a provider-staged complete-checkpoint import creates its destinations already available from host bytes. Those destinations are never evaluated or fenced, so staging does not wait on the MLX process-wide evalLock held by another request's prefill chunk. The head text does not describe or change the SSD cache's storage, crypto or admission behavior. It is documentation of a code change in CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift and ssd-kv-cache.md, neither of which is in this batch.

Threat context: T-041 (SSD prefix cache, TB-007, A-001) already covers the cache. The documented change affects availability and timing and does not touch the at-rest posture: HMAC names, AES-GCM, TTL and the salt scope are untouched. One possible side effect is a TTFT observation channel, since staging no longer waits on another request's prefill. The same-account oracle is already accepted as SEC-035, and this PR gives no evidence that it changes.

No security-relevant code is visible, so there is no finding. The code in CompleteCheckpointTransfer.swift is not supplied. A later review pass should verify that host-byte-backed, unfenced destinations still go through the same authenticated decrypt and binding checks, the same GlobalKVCacheBudget staging reservation and the same release paths. The doc claim itself is unverified.
